island: Minjerribah / North Stradbroke Island, Quandamooka Country, Queensland, Australia
coordinate_order: lat, lon as separate named fields
about: Getting to, from and around Minjerribah. There is no bridge and no scheduled air service, so every person, every vehicle, every crate of milk and every ambulance patient crosses Quandamooka (Moreton Bay) on a boat with a published timetable and a hard capacity. That single fact is the throttle on every other system in this world: population, trade, waste, health, emergency response, housing and mood. Model the ferry first and everything else inherits its shape.
honesty: Timetables in this pack are dated snapshots, not a live feed. The vehicle ferry, water taxi and bus timetables were captured in Luke's own straddie-night-market-lab repo on 11 May 2026 and re-checked against operator and Translink pages on 7 August 2026. Operators change services without notice. Never present a time in this file to a player as today's departure.

Every fare carries its own confidence and effective date. The vehicle ferry uses airline-style dynamic pricing, so a single number is always wrong. Where the only figure available came from a reseller rather than the operator it says so, because resellers add margin.

Vessel capacities, check-in rules, cancellation terms and freight restrictions are from the operator's own published documents and are high confidence. Queue lengths, wait times, marshalling capacity and demand curves are not. They are modelling constructs and every one of them is flagged.

The Toondah long weekend scenario is a model, not a measurement. Nobody has published vehicle counts, standby numbers or wait times for that terminal. The scenario shows its arithmetic so a local can correct one input and watch the rest move.

Road segment geometry is not repeated here. It lives in data/geography.json, sourced from OpenStreetMap. This pack adds the operating attributes: speed limit, surface behaviour, capacity constraint and failure mode.

Speed limits are the published island maximum plus township defaults. Only the two beach speed limits are individually sourced. Do not treat a per-segment limit in this file as signposted unless its speed_limit_basis says 'published'.

Nothing cultural is asserted here. Business and place names are recorded as their operators publish them. No name is translated or interpreted. That belongs in data/lore.json and docs/CULTURAL-REVIEW.md, and QYAC is the authority, not this file.

confidence_scale.high: Stated in an operator's own published document, a government or Translink page, or a legal terms and conditions document. Directly checkable.
confidence_scale.medium: Stated in a credible secondary source, a reseller, a tourism body, or a government source read at one remove. Or a figure that is dated and may have moved.
confidence_scale.low: Plausible and useful for simulation, but not verified for this island or this operator. Treat as a placeholder a local can correct.

structural_facts.claim: There is no bridge to Minjerribah. Every vehicle, every person and all freight crosses by boat, or on a private aircraft into the Dunwich airfield.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: Set a hard daily import and export ceiling equal to the sum of scheduled sailings times their capacity, minus crew and vehicle deck losses. No system may exceed it. If a system needs more, it has to buy an extra sailing or wait for tomorrow.

structural_facts.claim: On the North Stradbroke Island route, walk-on freight is permitted on the passenger ferry service only, may travel unaccompanied, and is charged at a per item rate. This is the reverse of the Southern Moreton Bay Islands route, where walk-on freight goes on the vehicle ferry and must be accompanied.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: Small parcel and unaccompanied goods flow follows the passenger ferry timetable, not the barge timetable. Anything big goes in a vehicle or a truck on the barge.

structural_facts.claim: SeaLink SEQ reserves the right to prioritise travel for emergency service vehicles and passengers as required.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: An ambulance or fire appliance displaces booked vehicles from a sailing. Model the displacement: two to four booked cars roll to the next boat, and the affected drivers get an unhappiness event that is not the operator's fault.

structural_facts.claim: The SeaLink long term car park at Toondah Harbour, on the corner of Middle Street and Emmett Drive behind the terminal, holds bays on a permanent long term basis for standard vehicles up to 5.4 m long and 2.0 m wide. Demand is high enough that there is a waitlist measured in years, not months. It is not a secure car park.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: A household with a mainland car and a long term bay has a different, much cheaper and faster mainland trip than a household without one. Make the bay an inheritable, tradeable household asset with a multi-year queue, not a purchase.
structural_facts.note: The waitlist length was read twice on 7 August 2026 and returned two different figures, longer than a year and longer than 4 years. The page appears to have been updated between reads. Use 'years' and do not state a number. The existence of the waitlist, the vehicle size limit and the not-secure disclaimer were consistent across both reads.

structural_facts.claim: The base vehicle ferry timetable is two vessels in a clean alternating loop. Each Cleveland departure is followed about an hour later by the same vessel departing Dunwich. Verified by reconstructing the published timetable: Minjerribah runs Cleveland 06:00, Dunwich 07:00, Cleveland 08:00, Dunwich 09:00 and so on, with Sea Breeze offset one hour behind.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: One vessel going mechanical removes roughly half the day's vehicle capacity, not a single sailing. This is the single most damaging non-weather failure in the world and it should be modelled as a cascading day, not an incident.
structural_facts.source: derived from the published timetable in repo-night-market, cross-checked against https://stradbrokeisland.com/getting-here/by-ferry/
structural_facts.note: DERIVED. The rotation is an inference from the times, not a statement by the operator. It holds exactly for every sailing in the base timetable.

structural_facts.claim: Public holidays, school holidays, Fridays and Sundays are the busiest times to travel.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: The demand curve is not a smooth seasonal sine wave. It is a weekly sawtooth with a Friday out spike and a Sunday back spike, multiplied by the holiday calendar.

structural_facts.claim: The two walk-on water taxi operators run to almost exactly the same times. Visit Straddie states plainly that both walk-on water taxis operate an identical timetable. Checked departure by departure, the eastbound times match minute for minute and the westbound times match on every departure except two in the afternoon, where the Flyer runs 16:45 and 18:00 against SeaLink's 17:00 and 18:15.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: They compete head to head on the same departures to two different Dunwich landings, so the choice a walk-on passenger makes is mostly about which side of Dunwich they want to arrive at, not about time. The one place time matters is the two afternoon departures where the Flyer goes fifteen minutes earlier.
structural_facts.note: Luke's 11 May 2026 snapshot recorded a different Flyer timetable, offset ten minutes (04:55, 05:55, 06:55 and so on). Three current sources now agree on the identical times. Treat the ten minute offset as stale. A local who catches the Flyer weekly will settle this in one sentence.

structural_facts.claim: Students travelling to and from school on the passenger ferry under the Translink School Travel Assistance Scheme must present a Student Travel Pass.
structural_facts.consequence_for_sim: Secondary school students are a fixed, non-negotiable weekday passenger block on the first morning and mid-afternoon passenger sailings. They do not respond to price and they cannot be shifted. Model them as inelastic demand that has priority claim on seats.

variants.day_restriction_conflict: Luke's 11 May 2026 snapshot marks the 06:00 Cleveland and 07:00 Dunwich sailings Monday to Saturday only, and the late evening pair Sunday only. The Sunday-only reading is used here because it comes from the cleaner snapshot, but a Friday evening barge is exactly the sort of thing a long weekend depends on, so check it before modelling a Friday night arrival.

cancellation.under_48h_before_departure: A$10 fee per one way journey, remaining value held as credit for 12 months from booking creation

booking.vehicle_dimension_rule: Declared dimensions must include any load that changes the length, width or height. Trailer length is measured from the towball to the end of the loaded unit. SeaLink may refuse boarding where dimensions were declared incorrectly.
booking.bicycles: Push bikes carried at no extra cost, subject to available space
booking.animals: Allowed on terminals and ferries. Dogs outside an enclosed cabin must be muzzled and leaded. Livestock such as goats and pigs not carried on passenger ferries and must travel in a vehicle.

fare_aud.pricing_model: Airline style dynamic pricing for vehicles, flat rates for walk-on passengers. A single number is always wrong; model a fare band that moves with load.

resident_flat.note: Announced by SeaLink with the State Member for Oodgeroo. Reported as a saving of A$31 on the previous average standard car fare, a reduction of 35 per cent. The end date is reported differently in different sources (31 March 2026 in one, 31 March 2027 in another); do not rely on it.

visitor_vehicle_reseller_quote.note: A reseller price, so it may carry a margin over the operator's own fare, and it is a snapshot of a dynamic price. Use it as an upper band, not as the fare.

multi_trip.note: SeaLink states the 30 return ticket brings the cost down to about A$6 per trip, a saving of more than 50 per cent on the standard fare. Which fare that is measured against is not stated.

fare_aud.payment: Visa, MasterCard and American Express carry a 1 per cent surcharge. PayPal, direct deposit, EFTPOS and cash are surcharge free.
fare_aud.effective_note: SeaLink states prices effective from 1 July 2026. The full fare table could not be read: sealink.com.au returns HTTP 403 to an automated fetch.

freight.walk_on_freight_rule: North Stradbroke Island walk-on freight is permitted on the passenger ferry service only, may travel unaccompanied, and is charged at a per item rate.
freight.handling_rule: All freight items must be able to be carried by one person and large items must be secured to a trolley. Freight quantities are limited and SeaLink may refuse carriage when the freight area is full.
never_carried_as_walk_on: furniture including lounge chairs and beds
timber, pipe or conduit longer than 3.0 m
cubby houses and animal enclosures over 1 cubic metre
off_peak_or_masters_discretion: tradesperson's tools such as welders and large toolboxes
small hot water system secured on a trolley
small fridge or freezer up to 280 litre, washing machine or clothes dryer secured on a trolley
timber, pipe or conduit under 3.0 m
lawn mowers, whipper snippers, portable generators and outboard motors, empty of fuel, on vehicle ferries only
two 20 litre approved fuel containers per passenger, on vehicle ferries only
freight.large_freight: SeaLink operates vehicle and passenger ferry services and directs customers to a local transport operator for large freight and furniture deliveries.
freight.consequence_for_sim: A household that buys a fridge or a couch cannot bring it home on a walk-on ticket. It needs a vehicle deck slot or a carrier. That is a real, common, expensive island friction and it should generate errands, costs and delays in the sim.

reliability.mechanism: The crossing is inside the bay so ocean swell is not the driver. Strong wind raises short bay chop across the exposed reach between the Toondah channel and Rainbow Channel, which slows the vessel and can suspend loading of high-sided vehicles.
reliability.modelled_effect: Above a modelled 25 knot sustained wind, add 5 to 12 minutes to the crossing. Above 35 knots, model a cancellation probability rising with wind speed.
reliability.note: No published wind threshold for this route was found. The operator's terms only say services are subject to alteration, sometimes without notice, including for adverse weather.

reliability.mechanism: Not a factor on this crossing. Minjerribah and Moorgumpin shelter the whole route from ocean swell.
reliability.modelled_effect: none. Do not add a swell term to the vehicle ferry. Swell belongs to the beaches, the bar and the offshore boats.

reliability.mechanism: Both terminals sit in shallow, dredged water. The Toondah channel needs maintenance dredging.
reliability.modelled_effect: unknown
reliability.note: Whether the vehicle ferry has any tidal restriction at Toondah or at the Dunwich apron could not be verified. Do not model a tide gate on the barge until a local or the operator confirms one. Tide restrictions on beach driving are separate and are verified; see beach_driving.

reliability.mechanism: Two vessels run the base timetable in an alternating loop. Losing one halves the day.
reliability.modelled_effect: A vessel out of service removes its five daily sailings each way, roughly 260 to 300 car slots. Bring Quandamooka in from the third-vessel role with a modelled 4 to 12 hour lead time, and until it arrives the backlog rolls forward day on day.

reliability.mechanism: Booked out sailings on a peak Friday, with a standby queue that has no reservation to fall back on.
reliability.modelled_effect: See scenario toondah-long-weekend-friday.

reliability.mechanism: Winter morning fog on the bay.
reliability.modelled_effect: unknown
reliability.note: Plausible but not confirmed as a cause of cancellations on this route. Left as a named unknown rather than a modelled term.

queue_model.summary: Two queues, not one. A booked queue that is orderly and a standby queue that is not.

stages.description: Vehicles book online days ahead. Peak Friday afternoon sailings sell out first, then Sunday and Monday afternoon returns.
Booked vehicles arrive at Toondah, most in the 20 to 60 minute window before their sailing, some much earlier hoping to roll forward onto an earlier boat.
Check in window. Booking number checked, driver directed to a marshalling lane. Check in closes 20 minutes before departure and late vehicles can be refused.
Vehicles wait in lanes by sailing. When the lanes fill, the queue backs out of the yard onto Middle Street.
stages.note: UNVERIFIED. No published lane count or yard capacity. This is the single number in this pack most likely to be wrong and it drives the whole spillover behaviour.

stages.description: Loading. Drivers accept crew direction, engines off once under way.
Unbooked vehicles and rollers wait for no-shows and unsold slots to be released at the check-in cut. This is where the anger lives.
stages.note: A no-show forfeits 100 per cent of the fare, which is a strong incentive to turn up. Keep the rate low.

priority_order: booked vehicles checked in before the cut
rollers with a later booking on the same day

reliability.modelled_effect: Total island taxi supply is 2 vehicles. On a Saturday night after the pub, or when the last bus has gone, demand exceeds supply by a wide margin and people walk, drive, or do not go. This is one of the clearest hard caps in the world and it should be visible to the player.

reliability.mechanism: One wheelchair accessible vehicle on the whole island.
reliability.modelled_effect: If that vehicle is booked or off the road, accessible road transport on Minjerribah is zero. Model it as a single point of failure with real consequences for a resident, not as a rounding error.

services.note: Status is trading-unconfirmed, carried forward from businesses.json. Described as operating for over 40 years. Confirm it is still running before showing it to a player.

services.name: StradEasy
services.description: Booked ferry-to-door transport meeting the boats at both Dunwich landings, plus charter for groups, weddings, conferences and school trips.

fare_aud.note: Not published. Booking by phone or web form.

services.role_in_sim: The fallback when the bus does not go where someone is staying, when a party is too big for the cab, or when the last bus has gone. Model it as bookable, finite and priced above the bus.

services.name: Scooters On Straddie
services.description: Scooter and car hire with a courtesy bus for pickup and drop-off. Positioned as the way to reach Brown Lake, Myora Springs and Amity Point without a long walk or a bus wait.

services.operator: North Stradbroke Airfield Pty Ltd operates the airfield; no scheduled carrier

reliability.modelled_effect: Wet weather closes the strip to some aircraft types.

reliability.mechanism: Kangaroos, wallabies and birds on the runway, worst at early morning and late afternoon.
reliability.modelled_effect: A real strike hazard at exactly the hours a medical flight is most likely.

reliability.mechanism: Turbulence and wind shear on approach to runway 15 in strong southerly and south-easterly winds.

services.role_in_sim: The quiet third door. It carries almost nobody, but it is the difference between a two hour and a twenty minute medical transfer, and it is why the island is not quite as cut off as the ferry timetable makes it look.

services.name: Private boats and the Amity Point and Dunwich ramps
services.description: A significant share of island movement never touches a timetable. Residents and mainland boat owners cross under their own power to the Amity Point boat ramp, the Dunwich ramps and private moorings.

capacity.note: No count of registered vessels, ramp movements or mooring holders was found for this island.

reliability.mechanism: Crossing the bay in a small boat is weather dependent in a way the barge is not.
reliability.modelled_effect: This channel closes first and reopens last.

services.role_in_sim: Model it as an uncounted background flow with a weather gate, not as a service. It is how a certain kind of islander opts out of the ferry economy entirely.
services.source: general knowledge, corroborated by the Redlands Disaster Plan which names the Amity Point boat ramp and One Mile Jetty as assembly areas

services.name: Island freight carriers
services.operator: multiple; Stradbroke Island Carriers is the named island carrier found
services.description: Commercial freight, building materials, whitegoods and furniture that cannot travel as walk-on freight move by truck on the vehicle ferry, booked through a carrier.

capacity.note: No fleet, load or frequency figure was found. A semi-trailer combination at about 19 m occupies a large share of a vehicle deck, so a single truck booking displaces many cars.

reliability.modelled_effect: On peak days freight and visitors compete directly. A busy long weekend pushes deliveries to Tuesday, which is why the shops run thin by Sunday night.

services.role_in_sim: The supply chain for every business in businesses.json runs through this. Stock levels on the island should be a function of vehicle deck slots won, not of demand.

road_segments.name: East Coast Road

hazards.source: https://stradbrokeisland.com/about-stradbroke/wildlife/ names car strike as a threat and advises driving under the limit at dawn and dusk; data/ecology.json records vehicle strike as the top ranked recorded koala mortality cause on the island, 35 deaths 1997 to 2010

road_segments.role: Dunwich main street off the ferry terminal end. Every vehicle that lands on this island drives up this street.

permit.requirement: All vehicles entering the Recreation Reserve on Minjerribah require a current Vehicle Access Permit. A 4WD and a permit are needed to reach the beach camping areas on Flinders Beach and Main Beach.

price_aud.note: CONFLICTING. One secondary source gives A$53.65 for up to one month and A$160.80 for more than one month up to one year. Another gives A$55.90 for one month. The Minjerribah Camping permit page itself shows prices only inside its booking system, which could not be read. Both figures are recorded so a local can strike out the wrong one.

flinders_beach.tide: no driving 2 hours either side of high tide

tide_rule_conflict.issue: Three different tide windows are published for the same beaches.

values.window: 2 hours either side of high tide
1 hour 15 minutes either side of high tide
1 hour either side of high tide

tide_rule_conflict.resolution: Use 2 hours. It comes from the body that issues the permit and enforces the condition, and it is the most conservative. The other two are recorded rather than deleted so a local can say which is signposted.

simulation_hook.description: Beach driving is the clearest tide coupling in the world. Read data/geography.json for the beach routes and the tide system for the water level, and open or close both beaches on the 4 hour window around each high tide.
simulation_hook.effect: Two closed windows per day, each about 4 hours, sliding roughly 50 minutes later each day. Camping traffic on Flinders and Main Beach clusters hard against the edges of those windows, so beach access points surge just after a beach opens.
simulation_hook.basis: derived from the published tide rule plus the standard semi-diurnal tide cycle

emergency_transport.principle: Every serious medical case leaves the island by boat or by air. There is no hospital on Minjerribah. The transfer time, not the treatment, is the thing the simulation should make a player feel.

transfer_paths.description: Ambulance drives onto the next vehicle ferry with priority boarding, displacing booked vehicles. 45 to 50 minute crossing plus the wait for the next sailing plus the mainland run to hospital.

transfer_paths.note: The worst case is an incident just after the last sailing of the day. On a Monday to Saturday the last Dunwich departure is 17:30 and the next is 07:00, a gap of 13.5 hours in which the barge is not an option at all.

Aeromedical helicopter to a Brisbane hospital.

evacuation.coordinator: Redland City Local Disaster Management Group
assembly_areas: the boat ramp at Amity Point
evacuation.transport_used: East Coast Road as the primary land route, with 4WD beach access from Point Lookout to Amity Point as the alternate; barge and ferry from Dunwich and Amity Point to Cleveland; the island bus service, the taxi and courtesy buses from the Rugby League Club and the Bowls Club
evacuation.public_information: ABC 612 AM, Bay FM 100.3 and council channels

scenarios.name: The Toondah queue on the Friday of a long weekend
scenarios.status: MODELLED. Not measured. Read the inputs table before using any number here.
scenarios.why_it_matters: This is the island's defining crowd scene and the moment its whole economy becomes visible as a physical line of cars. It is also the cleanest teaching moment in the simulation: a fixed supply of steel decks meeting an elastic demand, with a 20 minute cut-off and a 100 per cent no-show penalty doing all the interesting behavioural work.

measured.name: base Cleveland to Dunwich sailings, Friday
measured.source: published base timetable in this pack

measured.name: base daily westbound capacity
measured.derivation: five Minjerribah sailings at 52 plus five Sea Breeze sailings at 60

measured.name: island visitors, most recent published year

assumed.name: extra Quandamooka sailings westbound on the long weekend Friday
assumed.reason: SeaLink publishes peak timetables per period and uses Quandamooka for extras. Five is a plausible day for a third vessel on a 45 to 50 minute crossing with turnarounds. Replace with the real published peak timetable when one is to hand.

assumed.name: vehicles presenting westbound across the day
assumed.reason: A normal Friday is modelled at about 85 per cent of the 560 slots, roughly 476 vehicles. A long weekend Friday is modelled at 2.2 times that.

assumed.name: Toondah marshalling yard capacity before the queue spills onto Middle Street
assumed.reason: UNVERIFIED. No lane count or yard capacity is published. This single number drives all the spillover behaviour and is the first thing to correct.

assumed.name: share of capacity sold in advance
no-show rate
assumed.reason: Kept low because a no-show forfeits the whole fare.

assumed.name: early arrivals hoping to roll onto an earlier sailing

outcomes.carried_derivation: 1050 presenting minus 820 slots equals 230 who do not get across on the Friday
outcomes.booked_derivation: 820 slots times 0.92 sold in advance equals 754
outcomes.slots_released_derivation: 754 booked times a 3 per cent no-show rate equals about 23 slots released to standby across the day, roughly one and a half per sailing
outcomes.standby_success_derivation: 23 released slots plus about 43 unsold slots on the two earliest sailings, shared among 230 hopefuls

modelled_day.eastbound_mirror: The same shape runs in reverse on the Monday afternoon, and it is worse, because a visitor who misses the last Monday sailing loses a day of work rather than a day of holiday. Model Monday 13:00 to 17:30 eastbound with the same arithmetic and a higher unhappiness weight per hour waited.

second_order_effects: The Dunwich end floods in 45 to 50 minute pulses of 52 to 60 vehicles onto Junner Street. On this day there are 15 pulses instead of 10 and the last one lands at 19:20.
The 230 who do not get across spend money in Cleveland, not on the island, or go home. Some rebook for Saturday, which pushes the Saturday queue up before the Friday one has cleared.
Freight loses. Trucks are long and every metre of deck sold to a car is a metre not sold to a delivery. Shops run thin by Sunday and the restock lands Tuesday.
The taxi and StradEasy demand spikes at Dunwich, against a total island supply of two cabs and a small transfer fleet.

Route 880 is meeting boats that are now 50 per cent more frequent than the timetable it was written against. Every extra sailing either has a bus or does not, and if it does not, 200 foot passengers are standing at Junner Street with luggage.
Campground check-in at Minjerribah Camping and the 4WD permit counter take the whole arrival wave at once, and Flinders and Main Beach are on a tide gate at the same time.
Any emergency vehicle movement on this day displaces booked cars from a sold-out sailing, which is the one time the priority rule is visible and resented.
scenarios.how_to_falsify_this: Stand at Toondah on the Friday before a long weekend with a clicker and a phone. Count vehicles presenting per hour, count the lane capacity, ask the check-in staff what proportion of the day was standby, and time the longest wait. Four hours of counting replaces every assumed number above.
scenarios.confidence_reason: Every measured input is high confidence. Every demand and queue number is modelled. The scenario is arithmetically consistent and structurally right; the magnitudes are guesses until somebody counts.

projects.name: Dunwich (Gumpi) Ferry Terminal Upgrade
projects.status: funded, concept design released for community input, consultation closed 21 June 2026

funders.note: The three-way split was returned by a search of the TMR and State Development project pages. Neither page could be fetched directly (both return HTTP 403) and the figures were not repeated in the local news coverage that could be read. Confirm before quoting.

projects.scope: Concept design elements Council supports: a dual-berth passenger ferry pontoon, safer pedestrian links, improved vehicle and bus access, on-site parking and kiss and ride, sheltered waiting areas, landscaping, community open space and retail provision. Identified as a catalyst project under the Gumpi Master Plan.
projects.council_position: Council supports consolidating public ferry services into one primary location and says the facility must be designed from the outset to accommodate multiple ferry operators. Council has also said any closure of the One Mile terminal should only proceed after the Gumpi Master Plan commitments are met, including all-weather capability and sufficient parking.
projects.role_in_sim: A real, funded, currently undecided civic lever with a genuine trade-off already articulated by the people who will decide it. Single hub removes the two-landing confusion and simplifies bus scheduling. It also takes the water taxi arrival away from One Mile, and Council has already named the conditions (all weather, enough parking) under which that would be acceptable. Model those two conditions as gates on the lever, not as flavour text.

projects.name: Toondah Harbour Priority Development Area, Cleveland
projects.status: development partner withdrawn, PDA still in place, no clear pathway forward as at April 2026
projects.history: A federal assessment under the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act was the defining hurdle. A proposed refusal in April 2024 on unacceptable environmental impacts led Walker Group to withdraw its application. A smaller land-based revised concept never progressed to formal approvals. On 24 April 2026 Redland City Council acknowledged the withdrawal of Walker Group as development partner and said it would keep working with the Queensland Government, the majority landowner in the precinct.
projects.relevance: This is the mainland end of the island's front door. A terminal upgrade at Cleveland is a longstanding community ask and it is not funded or scheduled.
projects.role_in_sim: Mark the Toondah marshalling yard as unimproved and unfunded. The queue scenario above is not a temporary problem waiting on a project; it is the steady state.

reads: calendar (for school holidays, public holidays and long weekends)
publishes: transport: per-service next departure, load, delay state, queue length, and the island's current import and export ceiling
simulation_hooks.determinism_note: Every stochastic term in this pack (arrival jitter, no-shows, breakdown, wind) must draw from world.rng.stream('transport'). Never Math.random. Timetable lookups must use world.clock, never Date.now.
simulation_hooks.player_legibility: The one number a player should always be able to see is how many vehicle deck slots are left today. Everything else in this pack is downstream of it.
